content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines lean beef, tofu, and vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens). It is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, vitamin C, fiber, and essential minerals, while containing no potatoes or soy‑based sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.
Tofu is made from soybeans, but this recipe uses it without soy sauces, reducing sodium content.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound with documented anti‑cancer properties.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale) provide large amounts of vitamin K and folate.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Beef and tofu supply a complete set of essential amino acids that aid muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and carrots enhances the body’s defensive mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Beta‑carotene and sulforaphane neutralize free radicals, slowing aging processes.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Choosing lean cuts of beef reduces risk, but overconsumption can still raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to soy.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If salt or ready‑made seasonings are added, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear lean beef pieces until browned, add cubed tofu and lightly fry. Then stir‑fry sliced carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens for 5‑7 minutes until tender. Season with black pepper, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Freezing is not recommended, as the texture of beef, tofu, and vegetables may change.
